comparisons.coverage_method: Parsed the complete pinned manifest and all 135 indexed files: 130 BDDL definitions exactly match the static suite registry (10 spatial, 10 object, 10 goal, 10 LIBERO-10, 90 LIBERO-90), with five registry/predicate files. Verified every local file exists and matches its manifest SHA-256; no missing, duplicate, or mismatched files. Searched the complete definition inventory for adjustment, turning, locking, fastener, articulated-motion, and retention mechanisms, then read the closest BDDL and TurnOn predicate completely.
comparisons.objective: Candidate sets a gripper opening stop to 90°, locks that setting with a jam nut, and verifies retained opening over repeated cycles. LIBERO's nearest task only activates a stove.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires coaxial driver seating, wrench seating, coupled countertorque, setting preservation, tool withdrawal, and later articulated verification. LIBERO requires direct stove-control manipulation; its predicate delegates to the stove object's turn_on state and contains no adjustment screw, locknut, counterholding, or retained-cycle test.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires angular accuracy, seated/retained nuts, three repeat cycles, at most 2° drift, and one second of hands-off clearance. LIBERO succeeds on the single Boolean goal Turnon(flat_stove_1).

closest_tasks.name: KITCHEN_SCENE3_turn_on_the_stove
closest_tasks.physical_skill: Manipulate the stove control sufficiently to change its on/off state.
closest_tasks.success_condition: The Turnon predicate for flat_stove_1 is true.
closest_tasks.reason: It is the closest LIBERO rotary-control task, but measures binary activation rather than setting and mechanically locking an adjustable stop against reaction torque and verifying retention.

comparisons.reason: The only relevant shared primitive is turning an articulated control; LIBERO has no coupled screw/jam-nut adjustment, bimanual counterholding, or hands-off cycle-retention outcome.

comparisons.coverage_method: Parsed the complete pinned manifest and all 381 indexed files: 379 kitchen source files plus the environment initializer and dataset registry. Static parsing found 380 top-level kitchen task classes, including every adjustment/knob class exposed by the inventory. Verified every file against its manifest SHA-256 with no missing, duplicate, or mismatched files. Read the complete stove-task source, including its reset and backend success checks.
comparisons.objective: Candidate calibrates and locks a mechanical gripper opening stop, then tests whether the setting survives repeated motion. RoboCasa's nearest task adjusts a stove knob until it lies in a low-heat angular band.
comparisons.physical_skill: Both require angular regulation, but RoboCasa uses direct one-control knob rotation. Candidate additionally requires two concentric tools, counterholding during jam-nut tightening, regrasping/withdrawal, and operation of a separate articulated test lever.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires a retained 90° opening, seated nuts, three repeat cycles, bounded drift, and released clearance. LowerHeat succeeds whenever the selected stove knob's absolute joint value lies between 0.35 and STOVE_HIGH_MIN.

closest_tasks.name: LowerHeat
closest_tasks.objective: Lower a kettle burner's heat by adjusting its stove knob.
closest_tasks.physical_skill: Rotate one stove knob into a target joint-value band.
closest_tasks.success_condition: The knob value is within the defined low-heat interval.
closest_tasks.reason: This is RoboCasa's strongest target-angle neighbor, but it neither locks the setting with a coupled fastener nor tests hands-off retention after repeated mechanism cycles.

closest_tasks.name: TurnOnStove
closest_tasks.objective: Turn on a selected stove burner.
closest_tasks.physical_skill: Directly rotate a stove knob from off to an on state.
closest_tasks.reason: It shares rotary manipulation only; the outcome is binary activation with no screw/nut coupling, countertorque, setting preservation, or functional-cycle verification.

comparisons.reason: RoboCasa covers direct knob adjustment, including a target band, but not the candidate's central ability of preserving a calibrated screw position while locking a concentric jam nut and proving retained operation.

comparisons.coverage_method: Parsed the complete two-component manifest and all 11 indexed source files (two SimplerEnv registry/builder files and nine ManiSkill2-real2sim environment modules). Enumerated every registered environment and success function from those originals. Verified every file against its manifest SHA-256 with no missing, duplicate, or mismatched files, then read the complete nearest articulated-task definition.
comparisons.objective: Candidate adjusts and locks a gripper's maximum opening before testing repeated retained motion. SimplerEnv's nearest task opens or closes one cabinet drawer.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate combines precision tool seating, coupled countertorque, lock retention, tool release, and later lever actuation. OpenDrawer requires grasping/pulling a single prismatic drawer joint.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate grades angular accuracy, lock retention, repeated return, drift, and released clearance. OpenDrawer succeeds when the chosen drawer joint reaches qpos at least 0.15; CloseDrawer succeeds at qpos at most 0.05.

closest_tasks.name: OpenDrawerCustomInScene-v0
closest_tasks.physical_skill: Move one prismatic articulated joint beyond an opening threshold.
closest_tasks.success_condition: The target drawer joint reaches qpos ≥ 0.15.
closest_tasks.reason: It is the closest articulated-motion task in the complete registry, but measures one direct displacement rather than calibrated stop adjustment, counterheld locking, and repeated retained motion.

comparisons.reason: SimplerEnv includes articulated drawer movement but no fastener adjustment, bimanual lock reaction management, or post-lock functional retention test.

comparisons.coverage_method: Parsed both complete pinned definition sets and all 1,122 indexed files: 1,018 current BEHAVIOR-1K BDDLs, 101 legacy BDDLs, and three task/predicate backend files. Verified every file against its manifest SHA-256 with no missing, duplicate, or mismatched files. Searched all definitions for screw, bolt, nut, wrench, adjustment, locking, attachment, and articulated goals. The only fastener-word hits were tool-storage activities, so the closest assembly goal was make_cabinet_doors. Read that BDDL and the complete AttachedTo implementation because its abstract goal underspecifies the actual mechanism.
comparisons.objective: Candidate calibrates a gripper stop, mechanically locks it, and verifies retained motion. BEHAVIOR's nearest assembly task attaches a cabinet door to a cabinet base.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires coordinated driver/wrench countertorque and a subsequent articulated function test. make_cabinet_doors requires bringing attachment meta-links into positional/orientational alignment; the backend then creates a fixed or spherical joint.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires numeric angle accuracy, retained nuts, repeated cycles, bounded drift, and hands-off clearance. make_cabinet_doors succeeds when attached(cabinet_door, cabinet_base) is true; the backend attachment is selected within 5 cm and 15° before joint creation.

closest_tasks.name: make_cabinet_doors-0
closest_tasks.objective: Attach a cabinet door to a cabinet base.
closest_tasks.physical_skill: Align compatible attachment interfaces closely enough for the attachment state to create a joint.
closest_tasks.success_condition: The cabinet door's AttachedTo state identifies the cabinet base as its parent.
closest_tasks.reason: Backend inspection resolves this as meta-link alignment followed by joint creation, not screw adjustment or locknut counterholding; it also lacks an angle target and repeated functional-retention test.

comparisons.reason: BEHAVIOR contains a genuine assembly neighbor, but its tested ability is attachment-interface alignment; it does not test preserving an adjustable setting under locking torque or verifying that setting through repeated motion.

comparisons.coverage_method: Parsed both complete official JSON originals, verified their manifest hashes, and checked the authoritative task catalog: exactly ten published setup/instruction/reset/rubric records corresponding to the ten selected design IDs. Compared all ten complete published task records; unselected procedure candidates were not treated as benchmark tasks. Read the complete DC-knob record and its linked turn-knob industrial-procedure record.
comparisons.objective: Candidate sets and locks a robot-gripper opening stop, then verifies retained function. DC-knob rotates a fixed dimmer knob from a start mark to a goal mark.
comparisons.physical_skill: Both require target-directed angular motion. DC-knob is a single direct rotary manipulation; candidate adds coaxial driver and wrench seating, physical counterholding during locknut tightening, tool withdrawal, and separate repeated actuation.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires a precise retained angle, both nuts retained, three repeat cycles, bounded drift, and one second of released clearance. DC-knob awards full score when the knob line points at the goal mark and partial credit for noticeable clockwise progress.

closest_tasks.name: DC-knob — Turn the knob to the mark
closest_tasks.quote: The line on the knob points at the goal mark (turned clockwise to it).
closest_tasks.objective: Turn a rotary dimmer knob clockwise to a marked target.
closest_tasks.physical_skill: Directly rotate one knob to visual alignment with a mark.
closest_tasks.success_condition: Full credit at the goal mark, partial credit for clockwise movement that stops short, and zero for no clockwise progress.
closest_tasks.reason: This is the closest published target-angle task, but it has no adjustable screw plus jam nut, no need to preserve a setting against tightening reaction, and no repeated-cycle retention outcome.

comparisons.reason: DataCenterBench tests marked rotary positioning, but the candidate's central tested ability is mechanically locking a calibrated stop without disturbing it and proving hands-off retention across cycles.

comparisons.coverage_method: Parsed the complete pinned manifest and all 110 indexed files: 54 task modules, 54 matching task configurations, the shared _task.yml, and task_registry.py. Static pair checking found no task without a configuration and only the expected configuration-only _task template. Verified every file against its manifest SHA-256 with no missing, duplicate, or mismatched files. Searched the full task/config inventory and read both complete fasten_screws originals plus the dynamic registry.
comparisons.objective: Candidate adjusts one screw-defined gripper stop, locks it with a jam nut while preserving a target angle, and validates retained motion. RoboDojo fasten_screws inserts and tightens three color-matched screw/nut pairs.
comparisons.physical_skill: Both involve threaded hardware and tightening. RoboDojo emphasizes matching, coaxial insertion, and seating of separate fasteners; candidate emphasizes maintaining an already-coupled adjustment against jam-nut reaction with simultaneous driver/wrench counterholding, followed by mechanism cycling.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate grades opening angle, lock seating/retention, three return cycles, drift, and released clearance. RoboDojo grades one, two, or three matched pairs by nut uprightness, ≤1 mm XY alignment, ≥9 mm insertion depth, and open grippers.

closest_tasks.name: fasten_screws
closest_tasks.quote: Insert and tighten each screw into the nut of the same color.
closest_tasks.objective: Insert and tighten three screws into their color-matched nuts.
closest_tasks.physical_skill: Match separate fasteners, align their axes, insert them, and achieve sufficient depth.
closest_tasks.success_condition: Each pair is upright, aligned within 0.001 m in XY, inserted to the 0.009 m depth threshold, with grippers open for scored completion.
closest_tasks.reason: This is the strongest shared-fastener neighbor, but insertion/depth of separate screw-nut pairs does not test preserving a calibrated setting while tightening a concentric jam nut or verifying retained articulated function.

comparisons.reason: The suites share threaded-hardware manipulation, but their hardest tested abilities and outcomes differ: RoboDojo measures insertion/seating, while the candidate measures counterheld locking of an adjustment and post-release functional retention.
